Definition: Official suite or >=50 genuinely untouched width-256 networks with high-precision post-ReLU targets and exact implementation/cost accounting.
Implication for status: May support submission-readiness or high-confidence closure when the effect is large and mechanism-specific.

Definition: Local full repository, exact Kerdock/assets, >=24 fresh width-256 networks, reliable targets, frozen specification.
Implication for status: Can support strong continuation/closure decisions; protected holdout should remain separate.

Definition: Exact 66,048-row geometry or full-width networks, generally 8–23 networks, but sandboxed, synthetic, noisy, or incomplete runtime fidelity.
Implication for status: Useful evidence and falsification challenge; normally pause or close only the exact tested form.

Definition: Reduced width, reduced bases, surrogate Kerdock, or small synthetic sets.
Implication for status: Mechanism exploration only. Must not close a broad avenue.

Definition: Theorem, algebra identity, numerical exactness test, or toy simulation without challenge-scale performance.
Implication for status: Can prove algebra or impossibility, but not empirical MSE transfer.

Definition: Theorem-level impossibility or E4/E5 repeated decisive failure with strong margins and rescue attempts.
Implication for status: Mark Closed with explicit scope and reopen condition.

Definition: E3 decisive failure or E4 marginal failure; implementation quality credible but environment incomplete.
Implication for status: Close tested form or pause; do not generalize to the entire theoretical class.

Definition: E1/E2 evidence, N<12, synthetic-only, or unclear implementation provenance.
Implication for status: Record warning only; keep avenue open pending stronger local test.

Definition: Shipping; Leading/active; Open/bounded experiment; Paused/awaiting local validation; Closed tested form; Closed high confidence; Oracle mechanism only; Infrastructure.
Implication for status: Every row must use one of these and include a next action or reopen condition.

Definition: Canonical ratio is candidate MSE / baseline MSE, so lower is better. Inverse 'gain' reports must be converted or explicitly labeled.
A small or synthetic sandbox failure cannot by itself overrule stronger local work. Record environment, width, N, reference quality, and exact-geometry status.
Implication for status: Especially important for coresets, equivariant learning, micro-cubature, and sparse controls.
